details: PLAUSIBLE (not run: a paid bench). The brief allowed "the scenario/fixture text that makes a worker start", and the queue item's "What" says "the session delegates to a worker (as the delegate rule requires)"; the brief also says the graders' meaning is not decided. The fix changes the meaning of delegated-to-a-worker without changing its code: the prompt now does what the rule was supposed to. No run tried the scaffold fix alone (05-47 already had the prompt sentence), so it is not known whether the sentence is needed at all: the original "started: none" may have come from the session being blocked in a primary checkout and doing the job in its own worktree.
Size: (a) 15 minutes plus about $1.50 of bench; (b) 10 minutes.

Question for the owner. The bench runs a scenario under two setups and grades the result; one grader, "delegated to a worker", checks that the main session handed the job to a cheaper builder agent. Until today no scenario ever did, partly because the test project was set up so that nobody could write in it. The fix does two things: it sets the test project up as a proper working copy (that alone lets files land), and it adds to the task text "hand the building to a worker agent". With that sentence, any setup, even the old one without the delegation rule, will likely hand the job over because it is told to; the grader then tells nothing about whether a setup's rules make it delegate. It still works for what the queue item wanted: comparing the builder's model (Sonnet $0.07 vs Haiku $0.01 in today's run).
(a) Recommended: drop the sentence, keep the working-copy fix, one paid run (about $1.50) to see whether the rules alone make it delegate; the grader keeps its meaning.
(b) Keep the sentence; the scenarios measure the builder's model and cost, and their comments say delegation is ordered, not measured.
evidence: git diff master...HEAD -- evals/scenarios/*/prompt.md: both gain "Hand the ... to a worker agent (typed, with a brief file) and have it work right here in this working copy, not in another worktree; no spec change or review is wanted here."

lib/relay_bench.py:299-313 agent_used: regex search over agent_type, so "worker" matches an unprefixed --agents worker
~/.relay/bench/2026-10-24T05-47-12Z results: prompt sentence already present in the first run; no scaffold-only run exists
failing_case: Both prompts now say "Hand the building/writing to a worker agent (typed, with a brief file) ... not in another worktree; no spec change or review is wanted here".

`relay bench active baseline-old --tag cheap`: baseline-old loads no delegation rule and no delegate plugin, but the bench still passes --agents with an unprefixed `worker`; told by the prompt to use one, its session would pass `delegated-to-a-worker` (agent_type regex "worker") just like active. Before the change this grader was meant to show the difference ("Measures whether the front delegates to a worker (not Opus itself)", add-function/scenario.toml:1-2; "The right setup sends it to a worker", small-script/scenario.toml:1-2). The same holds for docs/benchmark.md:33, a rules.load bench that could drop the delegation rule.
Expected (owner's choice): either the grader keeps telling a delegating setup from a non-delegating one, or the scenario comments say it no longer does.
fix_hint: Owner's choice; see the pass cases for each answer.
pass_cases: - Answer (a): add-function and small-script prompts carry no "worker agent" sentence; a paid bench `relay bench active --set models.build=haiku --tag cheap --runs 1` with only the scaffold fix shows delegate:worker started and both scenarios at 1.00 under active (if it does not, the delegation rule is what needs fixing, a queue item).

- Answer (b): the prompts keep the sentence; scenario.toml header comments of both scenarios say the worker is requested by the prompt and the grader checks it ran, not that the setup chose it; docs/benchmark.md says the bench cannot compare delegation between setups.
- Either way: tests/test_bench_worker.py asserts the chosen prompt text and the linked-worktree scaffold.
reason: Sentence gone from both prompts; tests/test_bench_worker.py:24 test_prompt_does_not_order_a_worker passes, fails at baseline; linked-worktree test at :39 passes.
findings.summary: the prompts now order a worker, so delegated-to-a-worker measures obedience to the prompt, not whether the setup delegates
